channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Rubio says Trump to 'analyze' global impact of Russia sanctions during pause
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday that President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sanctions and tariffs on Russia would last 60 days, as the move drew bipartisan criticism and raised fears in Ukraine that Washington could ease further restrictions on Moscow.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: ‘Standing up for democracy’: Atlanta ‘No Kings’ rally draws Trump critics ahead of midterms
item.description: “No Kings, Vote Now” was the theme of a rally in Atlanta, one of many organised across the US on Saturday. While many demonstrators denounced President Donald Trump’s policies, organisers said the rally was aimed at getting out the vote in the November 3 midterm elections and protecting democracy in America.
item.dc:creator: Leela JACINTO

item.title: Looters seize on massive French protests to raid and vandalise shops
item.description: Looters on Saturday seized the opportunity to raid and vandalise a host of shops and businesses across France – from bakeries and supermarkets to tech stores – as hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets to protest higher living costs and other grievances.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: 🔴 Live: Chaotic scenes as organisers of French protests claim 800,000 have taken to streets
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: India: Police crack down on New Delhi protests
item.description: Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, ‌who was detained on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Brazil: Amazon deforestation at 40-year low
item.description: In Brazil, deforestation in the Amazon has reached its lowest level in 40 years. President Lula is bolstering his environmental record just over a week before the second round of the presidential election, in which he faces Flávio Bolsonaro.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ukraine war: "Mothers of Kherson" opera opens in Poland
item.description: "Mothers of Kherson" has opened at Poland's National Opera. The performance was co-produced with New York's Metropolitan Opera and created in close association with Save Ukraine, a group helping to bring back Ukrainian children who remain in Russia. More than four years after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the opera aims to "reawaken" global interest in the war.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Protests in France: "Two fires broke out in Place de la République"
item.description: Police and protesters clashed in Paris and other French cities on Saturday, with smoke from fires and tear gas filling the air at demonstrations nationwide against high prices, ahead of elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron. "Two fires broke out in Place de la République," reports France 24's Antonia Kerrigan from the ground.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 🔴 Live: Protester’s hand blown off by police grenade as unions say half a million march across France
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US: Four killed in Oregon school shooting
item.description: The teenage gunman who shot dead three children and a teacher in an Oregon school was a former special needs student there, officials said Friday, as they praised the heroism of people who helped to shorten the rampage.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Protests in France: "Living conditions are too harsh"
item.description: Saturday’s mobilisation in France follows calls on social media to revive the Yellow Vests movement, which emerged in 2018 against social injustice. Student groups protesting since mid-September have urged supporters to join. We discuss this with our journalist on the ground, Antonia Kerrigan, and our guest, Paul Smith, head of Modern Languages at the University of Nottingham.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France: What's different about today's protests?
item.description: In France, protests are under way across the country this Saturday. Demonstrators are protesting against the high cost of living, as well as poor working and studying conditions. We discuss this with France 24's Jamie Smith-Maillet.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 🔴 Israeli settlers beat French mayor, attack European diplomatic cars in West Bank
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Israeli settlers attack European delegation convoy in West Bank, beat French mayor
item.description: Israeli settlers on Saturday attacked a convoy carrying a European delegation in the occupied West Bank, beating up a 78-year-old French mayor. While Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu – who is just days from a crucial election – described the incident as a "smear" campaign against Israeli settlers, France's top diplomat urged Israel to "urgently halt criminal violence".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: France: "We've seen extremely high tensions between protesters and law enforcement"
item.description:
Protesters across France called for street demonstrations on Saturday against rising living costs. France 24's Antonia Kerrigan reports from Paris.
"The march from here to Place de Clichy isn't set to start for another hour. However, we've seen it kicking off extremely early doors. It seems that what's happened is that police attempted to block the protesters from reaching Place de la République, and we saw the use of tear gas. We've seen people running with their masks on. We also saw the use of stun grenades."
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France: Students, unions and Yellow Vests unite against austerity
item.description: 190 000 people could demonstrate this Saturday in France. They called for street demonstrations Saturday against rising living costs, joining high school students' grievances over education conditions after more than three weeks of school blockades.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Will Paramount’s creation of Skydance test France’s cultural exception?
item.description: Skydance’s $110 billion creation tests whether France’s cultural exception can still compel a leveraged global media giant to fund, protect and prioritise French creativity, or merely treat it as a compliance cost.
item.dc:creator: Ella ARWYN JONES

item.title: Fires and clashes rock France amid massive nationwide protests
item.description: Protesters clashed with police in Paris and other French cities on Saturday as hundreds of thousands took to the streets to protest higher living costs and the declining conditions in schools and other public services. Several town halls were broken into – and in at least one instance set on fire – and many shops were vandalised and ransacked. One protester had his hand torn off by what appeared to be a crowd-control grenade used by police.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: 🔴 Live: Tens of thousands join protests across France, clashes reported in several cities
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France faces day of cost-of-living protests
item.description: French authorities detained dozens on Saturday at the start of nationwide protests against the cost of living, in what is likely to be a key indicator of the social climate heading toward elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron. France 24's Antonia Kerrigan tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Cameroonian journalist shot in Bamenda
item.description: Cameroonian journalist Ambe Macmillan is recovering in hospital after being shot in the legs by gunmen in the north-western city of Bamenda. A young woman was also killed as the attackers opened fire on mourners attending a wake. The shooting has renewed concerns about the dangers facing journalists in Cameroon's English-speaking regions, after years of conflict between government forces and separatist groups.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Uganda launches Ebola vaccine trial
item.description: The town of Masaka in southern Uganda is currently conducting a Phase 1 trial of a vaccine candidate against the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, which is circulating in the region. There is currently no approved treatment or vaccine for this strain.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Kenya reports third Ebola case, contact tracing continues
item.description: Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola, a relative of a man who died earlier this month after travelling from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The health ministry said the 65-year-old woman tested positive while in quarantine, where she has been since 5 October. The second patient, a 39-year-old man from the same family, is in a stable condition. Health officials say there is no evidence of community transmission, as both individuals were under quarantine. However, three contacts have yet to be traced. Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Russia hails Trump waiving sanctions as 'historic'
item.description: Russia on Saturday hailed US President Donald Trump's move to waive new sanctions on it as "historic", as Ukraine worries he is taking Moscow's side in Europe's worst conflict since World War II.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
